target_customer: California homeowners who want to split their lot and build or sell a new unit under SB9
problem: Homeowners lack the knowledge, capital and permitting help to use California's lot split and ADU rules to develop their property.
business_model: development services and financing for homeowners, fees on lot split and construction projects

founders.name: Samuel Schneider
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio.

founders.name: Sean Phillips
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio.

exit.reason: YC marks it Inactive but the website was still live in 2024 and says Homestead partnered with Yardsworth; no sale or shutdown is reported.

technical_complexity.rationale: Eligibility checker and workflow tooling were simple; the difficulty was permitting, construction and capital, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Expertise in local permitting could accrue, but contractors and other startups could replicate the service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SB9 only took effect January 1, 2022; other startups such as BuildCasa entered later and the Homestead site later carried a Yardsworth partnership banner.

market_need_then: California housing shortage and new lot and ADU rules; the YC pitch cited the SB9 regulatory opportunity, and a Terner Center brief estimated about 700,000 parcels could be split, though uptake in surveyed cities was thin in 2022 and 2023.

identity.voice_and_tone: Educational content hub with SB9 handbooks, city guides and a blog.

branding.community_and_virality: Dwell published an article about the company in June 2021 per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Educational content and a Dwell feature helped, but the name is generic and shared with many unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Homestead began as a platform to help homeowners become developers and focused on SB9 lot splits, reaching a team of 14 per the YC page. Seed funding is reported by aggregators with conflicting amounts and no shutdown reporting exists; the site later became an SB9 resource center with a Yardsworth partnership. The cause of the Inactive status is not public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Two seed entries conflict: CB Insights says about $150K on March 17, 2020 with YC and Brightlane Ventures; StartupIntros says $2M on May 1, 2020 with named angels. Each rests on a single database or outlet and they may describe the same raise. The site banner says Homestead partnered with Yardsworth and the footer reads Yardsworth 2024; no ownership change is confirmed. Competitors left empty: the SB9 competitor pages found (BuildCasa, KQED) are undated or from 2022 or later, too late for the Winter 2020 batch. YC founded year 2020; other sources say 2018 or 2019. Cause of inactivity not public.
